scope: governed merge-field boundaries, sensitive-value redaction, current-state snapshot resolution, partial-update preservation, finite comparison and serialization, significance-threshold validation, preview/write reconciliation, source immutability, and cross-product integrity
confirmed_findings_fixed: Merge previews previously discovered changes across almost every stored column and could expose arbitrary newly introduced upload fields and their raw values; change detection is now restricted to an explicit database-supported field contract.
Sensitive governed HR fields could expose raw before/after values in detailed merge previews; sensitive field changes now disclose that a field changed while suppressing the raw values.

Partial updates could silently overwrite omitted optional fields with NULL because the database upsert writes every supported column; update writes now coalesce omitted or missing incoming fields from the stored record unless a future explicit clear-field contract is introduced.
Non-finite numeric inputs could reach comparison or serialization paths; governed numeric fields normalize non-finite values to missing and preview serialization is strict JSON-safe.
Significance thresholds accepted invalid, negative, boolean or non-finite values; thresholds now require finite non-negative numeric values.
Snapshot merge inputs now resolve one latest record per employee and conflicting records sharing the same SnapshotDate fail closed rather than depending on row order.
Execute-merge now constructs writes only for added or genuinely changed employees and only from governed persistence fields.
Preview processing deep-copies input frames so source data remains unchanged.
interpretation_boundary: Merge previews are an authorized operational HR data-reconciliation surface, not analytics, prediction or employment-decision evidence. Redaction protects preview disclosure; access to the underlying persisted workforce data still depends on the application's authorization and local data-governance controls.
remaining_limits: Explicit field-clearing semantics are intentionally not implemented; a missing incoming value preserves the known stored value rather than being interpreted as an instruction to erase it.
Source-system definitions, HRIS reconciliation and upstream record authority cannot be inferred by MergeEngine and require organization-specific data contracts.
The local SQLite database remains a compatibility persistence layer; multi-writer transactional HRIS synchronization and distributed concurrency require separate integration validation.
Sensitive-field redaction at merge preview does not substitute for access control, filesystem security, retention policy or broader privacy governance.
